message.content:
You are an adversarial C++ reviewer for a cocos2d-x 3.17 physics module that CANNOT be compiled
in this environment (external deps absent). Your job is to catch anything that would break a real
build or produce wrong behaviour.

File under review: /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsCollisionPair.cpp
Its header: /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsCollisionPair.h
Chipmunk API version: 7 (with physics/cpCompat62.h providing 6.2-style aliases).

Implementer self-report: {"file":"/workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsCollisionPair.cpp","functions_implemented":30,"markers_remaining":0,"uncertain_identifiers":["cpArbiterGetCount","cpArbiterGetPointA","cpArbiterGetPointB","cpArbiterGetDepth","cpArbiterGetNormal","cpArbiterTotalImpulse","cpArbiterTotalKE","cpArbiterIsFirstContact","cpArbiterIsRemoval"],"notes":"All 30 declared methods implemented (ctor/dtor left as-is). Proven from in-tree call sites: cpArbiterGetShapes/CP_ARBITER_GET_SHAPES, cpShapeGetUserData, cpShapeGetBody, cpShapeGetSensor (CCPhysicsWorld.cpp), cpArbiterGet/SetRestitution, cpArbiterGet/SetFriction, cpArbiterGet/SetSurfaceVelocity, cpArbiterIgnore (CCPhysicsContact.cpp), cpBodyGetVelocityAtWorldPoint(body, cpVect) (CCPhysicsBody.cpp:508). The 9 listed identifiers are standard Chipmunk 7 public arbiter API but have no in-tree call site and external/ is not vendored, so they could not be verified against a header - worth a grep against the real chipmunk.h. Deliberate design decisions a reviewer should confirm: (1) per-point normalImpulse/tangentImpulse are the arbiter total impulse projected on normal/tangent divided evenly by contact count, because Chipmunk 7 exposes no public per-contact-point impulse accessor (jnAcc/jtAcc live in the private cpContact struct, and I avoided chipmunk_private.h and guessing struct fields). (2) getTotalNormalImpulse/getTotalTangentImpulse return std::fabs of the projection (magnitudes) - cpArbiterTotalImpulse is sign-flipped depending on arb->swapped, so a raw projection would usually be negative. getTotalImpulse still returns the signed vector. (3) CollisionPoint::depth stores the raw cpArbiterGetDepth value (Chipmunk reports penetration as negative); computeOverlap reports max std::fabs(depth) so it is positive and sign-convention agnostic. (4) computeRelativeVelocity = velocityB - velocityA at computeContactCenter(), so computeSeparatingVelocity is positive when separating given the Chipmunk normal points from shape A to shape B. (5) computeContactCenter averages the midpoint of pointA/pointB per contact. (6) getContactPoints writes getContactCount() entries and reports 0 in *outCount when outPoints is null (there is no capacity parameter in the header signature, so the caller must supply room for getContactCount() points; Chipmunk caps this at CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER). (7) update() delegates to init() and calls invalidate() on failure; invalidate() drops only _arbiter and _valid (shapes are retained but every accessor gates on _arbiter != nullptr and _valid). No new #includes were added; <cmath> was already present for std::fabs, matching the std::fabs style used in CCPhysicsHelper.cpp. Note CCPhysicsHelper.cpp (cpv2point/point2cpv/cpfloat2float) is being implemented concurrently by another agent - this file depends on those being correct."}

REVIEW CHECKLIST - be specific and skeptical:
1. Does every function definition exactly match its declaration in the header (name, params,
   const-ness, return type, class scope)? Any function declared in the header but now MISSING from
   the .cpp? Any function defined in the .cpp but not declared?
2. Does every Chipmunk symbol used actually exist in Chipmunk 7 (or in cpCompat62.h)? Flag any
   invented function, wrong arity, or wrong argument order. Confirm struct field names
   (cpSegmentQueryInfo{shape,point,normal,alpha}, cpPointQueryInfo{shape,point,distance,gradient},
   cpContactPointSet{count,normal,points[].pointA/pointB/distance}).
3. Does every cocos2d-x member/accessor used actually exist? Grep the relevant headers to confirm.
   Flag invented members.
4. Are all #includes present for what is used, and do all included paths exist on disk?
5. Any remaining "Hollowed in benchmark base" comment, or any function that still just returns a
   constant when real work is possible?
6. Correctness: null-guards, off-by-one in loops, integer/float division, uninitialised struct
   fields, dangling pointers, use of unordered containers where deterministic output order is
   required, missing retain/release, missing cpSpace lock guards.
7. C++ validity: balanced braces, missing semicolons, lambda-to-function-pointer conversions that
   will not compile (capturing lambdas can NOT convert to C function pointers - flag any capturing
   lambda passed to a Chipmunk callback), narrowing conversions, use of C++ features beyond C++11.
8. Does the file still compile-plausibly as a whole? Read it end to end.

Use Read/Grep freely. Then FIX every real problem you find yourself, directly in
/workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsCollisionPair.cpp (you may only modify that file). Re-read after editing to confirm.

RETURN a JSON object: file, issues_found (array of short strings), issues_fixed (array of short
strings), remaining_risks (array of short strings), markers_remaining (int), verdict
("clean" or "fixed" or "needs_attention").
